about: Seeded performance-engineering knowledge. Each entry is a diagnosis: what you see, when it applies, the cheap test that confirms it, the remedy, and how you know it worked. Edit or add entries freely — this file is data, not code. Add your own hard-won issues here; the agent will check every future script against them. Entries carrying a `fix` are REPAIRED automatically when their producer is provable in the recording; the rest are reported for a human.

entries.title: A dynamic value is hardcoded even though the recording shows where it comes from
entries.symptom: The script sends a long token/id as a recorded literal, and that exact value appears in an earlier response — so it was dynamic and is now stale.
entries.discriminate: Search the recording for the literal. If any earlier response contains it, it is server-issued, not a constant.
entries.remedy: Extract it from the producing response and reference it as a variable everywhere downstream. Reported only, never auto-applied: this pattern is a catch-all, and other passes deliberately leave some matching values alone (OAuth state/nonce, PKCE constants). A human decides.
entries.verify: Replay: the request now sends a value that differs from the recording and the step still succeeds.

entries.title: ASP.NET __VIEWSTATE / __EVENTVALIDATION not correlated
entries.symptom: Postbacks fail, redirect to the start page, or return a validation error, because ViewState is per-page and single-use.
entries.discriminate: Load the page twice in a browser and compare the hidden field values — ASP.NET regenerates them per render.
entries.remedy: Extract __VIEWSTATE, __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR and __EVENTVALIDATION from the GET that renders the form, and send them on the following POST. Keep them URL-encoded.
entries.verify: The postback returns the expected next page instead of bouncing back to the form.

entries.title: JSF javax.faces.ViewState not correlated
entries.symptom: JSF/PrimeFaces requests fail with a ViewExpiredException or silently return the same page.
entries.discriminate: The value changes on every page render, and the server keeps a per-session view map.
entries.remedy: Extract javax.faces.ViewState from each rendering response and send the freshest value on the next request. Server-side state saving also requires a stable session cookie.
entries.verify: No ViewExpiredException, and the partial-response XML reflects the action you submitted.

entries.title: SAML SSO assertion not correlated (auto-POST form)
entries.symptom: Login appears to succeed but the app never gets a session: the browser silently auto-POSTs a hidden SAMLResponse/RelayState form that a script must reproduce.
entries.discriminate: Look for an HTML form the browser submits via JavaScript on load, with the assertion in a hidden input — it is base64 and single-use.
entries.remedy: Extract SAMLResponse and RelayState from the IdP response body and POST them to the ACS URL as a real step. Do not follow redirects blindly through the handoff.
entries.verify: The ACS POST returns a session cookie for the service-provider domain.

entries.title: CSRF / anti-forgery token sent as a recorded literal
entries.symptom: Mutating requests fail with 403/419, or return the form again with a generic error.
entries.discriminate: Reload the form page — the hidden token changes. Some frameworks rotate it per request, others per session.
entries.remedy: Extract the token from the page that renders the form (hidden input or meta tag) and send it on the submit. If the framework also sends it as a header, set the header too.
entries.verify: The mutating request succeeds and the change is visible in a follow-up read.

entries.title: Not enough test data rows for the configured user count
entries.symptom: The script passes at 1 user, then produces lock contention, duplicate-record errors or unrealistic cache hits under load, because threads share the same few data rows.
entries.discriminate: Count rows in the CSV against the thread count. With shareMode=all and recycle, thread N+1 simply reuses row 1.
entries.remedy: Generate or supply at least one unique row per concurrent user (more for multi-iteration runs), or make the flow pick its entity from a live listing response instead of a fixed pool.
entries.verify: At the target user count, no two threads operate on the same business entity.

entries.title: App issues session cookies but the plan has no Cookie Manager
entries.symptom: Everything after login behaves as if logged out — often HTTP 200 serving the login page.
entries.discriminate: Check whether the recording's Set-Cookie values are ever echoed back on later requests.
entries.remedy: Add an HTTP Cookie Manager. Keep it per-thread so each virtual user holds its own session.
entries.verify: Post-login steps return real application content, not the login page.

entries.title: Load balancer session affinity — each user needs its own cookie store
entries.symptom: Load lands unevenly on one node, or throughput plateaus far below expectation, because every thread carries the same persistence cookie.
entries.discriminate: The cookie is set by the edge, not the app, and its value encodes a backend node.
entries.remedy: Ensure the Cookie Manager is per-thread (not shared). Decide deliberately whether to clear it per iteration — clearing re-balances, keeping it models a returning user.
entries.verify: Under load, backend nodes receive comparable request counts.

entries.title: Recording captured almost no response bodies — correlation is impossible
entries.symptom: Very few correlations are found and dynamic values ship as literals, no matter how good the tooling is.
entries.discriminate: A JMX holds only requests; the response side lives in the recording XML/JTL. If bodies are missing, there is nothing to extract from.
entries.remedy: Re-capture with response bodies enabled, or pair the JMX with the recording file that has them.
entries.verify: Body coverage is high and the correlation count rises accordingly.

entries.title: Script validates on HTTP status alone
entries.symptom: The run reports success while the application returned an error page, a login page, or an empty result — all with HTTP 200.
entries.discriminate: Open a passing response body and ask whether it actually contains the business outcome.
entries.remedy: Assert a business marker on each key step — a field the working response always carries — not just the response code.
entries.verify: Deliberately breaking the step (e.g. bad credentials) now fails the script.

entries.title: Extractor has no default value — failures become silent
entries.symptom: When the regex misses, the variable is empty and the next request sends a blank value, producing a confusing downstream error instead of an obvious one.
entries.discriminate: Look at the failing request: an empty or literal ${var} in the sent value means the extractor never matched.
entries.remedy: Give every extractor an obvious default such as NOT_FOUND so a miss is visible at the point it happens.
entries.verify: A forced miss shows the sentinel value in the request, at the right step.
